name: Patreon
tagline: Paid memberships, posts, chats, community, and creator discovery

pricing.native: Percentage of creator income plus processing
pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: No published cap on free or paid members/posts; 10% platform fee for creators who published after August 4, 2025; up to 100 native-video hours per month once there are paying fans.

pricing.freeTierCaps: No monthly fee and no published member/post cap; Patreon takes 10% of creator income under the current standard plan
pricing.billingTerms: percentage-of-income pricing; no monthly or annual subscription
pricing.hiddenCosts: Payment processing is commonly 2.9% + $0.30 for USD payments, plus payout fees and 2.5% currency conversion where applicable; qualifying iOS purchases can incur Apple's 30% fee, especially outside the US.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Patreon's durable value is payments, network, compliance, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a narrow membership platform storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Stripe account and API keys in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations
whyPeopleStillPay: Patreon: Creators pay to outsource payments, tax complexity, disputes, deliverability, moderation, and the trust needed to convert strangers.
ongoingBurden: Own payments, webhooks, refunds, tax records, fraud, access control, file delivery, moderation, backups, and support.

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: Paid communities, memberships, courses and posts in one self-hosted product; discovery remains your marketing problem.

facts.install: Docker Compose, with SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL set before first start
facts.dataFormat: Application records in MongoDB; production media uploads use MediaLit plus S3-compatible object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: CourseLit has no creator discovery network and its community/social experience is less mature than Patreon's.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker starts the app, but a production setup also needs SMTP for email login and MediaLit/S3-compatible storage for uploads

alternatives.name: Discourse
alternatives.desc: Paid groups, posts and chat with Stripe built in; there is no Patreon discovery feed to bring strangers.

facts.install: Use the official Docker installer on a 64-bit Linux server; managed Discourse hosting is the paid alternative
facts.dataFormat: Persistent records in PostgreSQL, Redis for cache/queues, and uploads/backups/logs in the Docker volume or S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Discourse has no creator discovery feed and is forum-first rather than a polished paid-content creator page.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a Linux VPS, Docker, DNS, TLS, working SMTP and regular upgrades

alternatives.name: Ghost
alternatives.desc: Paid posts, members and newsletters without Patreon's discovery, chats or audience hand-holding.

facts.install: Run Ghost-CLI on supported Ubuntu/MySQL hosting; the official Docker path is available but still documented as preview
facts.dataFormat: Posts, members and settings in MySQL; images under Ghost's content directory by default or through a configured storage adapter
facts.gapVsPaid: Ghost has no Patreon discovery network or native group chat, so audience acquisition and community conversation remain separate.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a server, domain, DNS, TLS and transactional/newsletter mail, plus Ghost upgrades

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Paid memberships, posts, community and email on a permanent free plan; it will not put you in front of Patreon's audience.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, funnels, course/community content, orders, emails and uploaded files in systeme.io's vendor-managed cloud; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: systeme.io provides no Patreon discovery network or creator feed that can bring an audience.
facts.setupBlocker: Selling requires connecting a payment gateway; the free plan is capped at 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, one community and one custom domain

rejectedAlternatives.name: Liberapay
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It is genuinely free, but intentionally offers donations with no rewards, gated posts, chats or community tiers.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Substack
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The product fits paid posts and community, but Substack takes 10% of every paid transaction before Stripe fees.

notes: Credibility row: Patreon survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Patreon; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + Stripe.
Primary job: Build a narrow membership platform storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations; native apps and community moderation; fulfilment, email, and affiliate ecosystems.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
